questions.cite: Variable-wind (dndndnVdxdxdx) group is reported clockwise; exact sectors depend on the unseen METAR.

questions.q: Visibility 1500 m is towards
questions.cite: Directional minimum-visibility indicator is read from the METAR string, which is unavailable.

questions.q: Visibility towards N is
questions.cite: Value depends on the directional visibility group in the actual METAR, not provided here.

questions.q: Height of base of low clouds above station level is
questions.cite: Cloud-base is decoded from the METAR cloud group (hundreds of ft above station); underlying report not present.

questions.q: Runway Visual Range is
questions.cite: RVR value comes from the R-group of the actual METAR, which is unavailable; option (a) is a cloud-amount value, not an RVR.

questions.q: The poor visibility is due to Present Weather which is
questions.cite: Present-weather cause is read from the ww group of the actual METAR, not provided here.

questions.q: Amount of CB cloud is
questions.cite: CB amount (oktas) is decoded from the METAR cloud group, which is unavailable.

questions.q: Height of base of CB is
questions.cite: CB base height is read from the METAR; underlying report not present, so value cannot be verified.

questions.q: The height of topmost layer of cloud is
questions.cite: Topmost cloud height is decoded from the METAR cloud groups (reported in ft), unavailable here; only the ft option is a valid form.

questions.q: The landing forecast appended to any METAR is valid for
questions.cite: A TREND (landing) forecast attached to a METAR/SPECI is valid for 2 hours from the report time.

questions.q: The wind in TREND from 0330 UTC is valid up to
questions.cite: End time of the FM/TL trend period is read from the specific TREND text, which is not present here.

questions.q: The difference between TT and TdTd is 3°C. The atmosphere is
questions.cite: A small temperature/dew-point spread (about 3°C) indicates near-saturated, moist air; 0°C spread would be saturated.

questions.q: Just before METAR issued
questions.cite: Recent-weather (RE) reading depends on the actual METAR string, which is not provided.

questions.q: Range of pressure as Q1003 is
questions.cite: QNH is rounded down to the whole hPa, so Q1003 covers 1003.0 to 1003.9 hPa.

questions.q: Temperature reported as 32°C is
questions.cite: Temperature is rounded to the nearest whole degree, so 32 represents 31.5 to 32.4°C.

questions.q: Visibility is reported in steps of 50 m when visibility is
questions.cite: Visibility is coded in 50 m steps from 0 up to 800 m.

questions.q: Visibility reported in steps of 100 m when visibility is
questions.cite: Visibility is coded in 100 m steps between 800 m and 5000 m.

questions.q: Visibility reported in steps of 1000 m when visibility is
questions.cite: Visibility is coded in 1000 m steps from 5000 m up to 9999.

questions.q: Visibility reported 9999 when visibility is
questions.cite: The code 9999 is used when visibility is 10 km or more.

questions.q: Temperature +2.5°C is reported as
questions.cite: Half-degree rounds up, so +2.5°C is reported as 03.

questions.q: Temperature −12.5°C is reported as
questions.cite: Negative temperatures use the M prefix; −12.5°C rounds to M12, and only the M-form is the valid METAR notation.

questions.q: Pressure rounded to nearest whole number in hectopascal
questions.cite: QNH in the pressure group is always rounded down to the next lower whole hPa.

questions.q: QNH 1002.6 hPa is reported as
questions.cite: QNH is rounded down to the whole hPa, so 1002.6 becomes Q1002.

questions.q: QNH 29.92 inches is reported as
questions.cite: Altimeter setting in inches uses the A prefix with hundredths, so 29.92 in is A2992.

questions.q: Fog is reported when visibility is
questions.cite: Fog (FG) is reported when visibility is less than 1000 m.

questions.q: Mist is reported when visibility is
questions.cite: Mist (BR) is reported when visibility is between 1000 m and 5000 m.

questions.q: CAVOK signifies Visibility, Cloud… and present weather better than the prescribed values or conditions
questions.cite: CAVOK stands for Ceiling And Visibility OK; the cloud element referred to is the ceiling.

questions.q: CAVOK is issued when visibility is
questions.cite: CAVOK requires visibility of 10 km or more.

questions.q: CAVOK is issued when: (i) Vis 10 km or more; (ii) No cloud below 1500m or below highest MSA; (iii) No CB.
questions.cite: CAVOK is used only when all three conditions (visibility, no low cloud, no CB/TCU and no significant weather) are met.

questions.q: SPECI is issued when
questions.cite: A SPECI is issued as soon as any single reporting criterion for change is met.

questions.q: SPECI is issued when Clouds are BKN or OVC base at 30, 60, 150, 300, 450 m AND cloud amount below 450m changes.
questions.cite: Either a BKN/OVC base crossing a threshold or a change in cloud amount below 450 m independently triggers a SPECI; the combined-condition phrasing is ambiguous.

questions.q: SPECI is issued for vertical visibility, by stations having Ceilograph, when sky is obscured
questions.cite: Stations equipped to measure vertical visibility issue SPECI for changes in VV when the sky is obscured.

questions.q: SPECI is issued when surface temperature has increased by
questions.cite: Temperature-change SPECI threshold varies by manual; the stored 2°C matches the common Indian text value but is not uniformly standardised.

questions.q: WSRWY28 indicates that the wind shear has been reported for
opts: both take off and approach paths
questions.cite: WS RWY28 denotes wind shear along runway 28, covering both the take-off and approach paths of that runway.

questions.q: R26/M0150 in a METAR indicates that
opts: 150 m is the lowest RVR instrument can measure and RVR < 150 m
questions.cite: Prefix M means 'less than'; 150 m is the lowest value the RVR instrument can assess, so actual RVR is below 150 m on runway 26.

questions.q: The TAF has been issued on
questions.cite: Answer depends on the specific coded TAF header not provided; stored value retained.

questions.q: The TAF has been issued at
questions.cite: Issue time read from coded TAF header not provided; stored value retained.

questions.q: The expected surface wind speed is
questions.cite: Wind group value read from the specific coded message not provided.

questions.q: Initially expected wind direction is
questions.cite: Initial wind direction read from the specific coded message not provided.

questions.q: TAF is Valid for Date
questions.cite: Validity date read from coded validity group not provided; stored value retained.

questions.q: Lowest forecast visibility in TAF is
questions.cite: Lowest visibility read from the specific coded message not provided.

questions.q: Height of base of lowest clouds in TAF is
questions.cite: Cloud group decodes in hundreds of feet; exact value from coded message not provided.

questions.q: Weather TSRA is expected after
questions.cite: Change-group onset time read from coded message not provided; TAF times are UTC.

questions.q: Direction of gusty wind is
questions.cite: Gust-wind direction read from coded change group not provided.

questions.q: Expected weather up to 2504 0400UTC is
questions.cite: Weather up to stated time read from coded message not provided.

questions.q: Period of validity of TAF is
questions.cite: Validity period read from coded validity group; TAF times are UTC.

questions.q: Group 1500/1509 in a TAF indicates
opts: TAF is valid from 15th 0000 to 0900 UTC
TAF is valid from 1500 to 0900 UTC
questions.cite: Validity group DDHH/DDHH: valid day 15 0000 UTC to 0900 UTC.

questions.q: What is true of a TAF?
opts: TAF valid for 9 hr is issued every 6 hr
TAF valid for 12–30 hr is issued every 3 hr
TAF for national use valid for 9 hr and issued every 3 hr
questions.cite: National TAF is valid 9 hr and issued at 3-hourly intervals.

questions.q: Time of issue of ROFOR is
questions.cite: Issue time read from coded ROFOR header not provided; times are UTC.

questions.q: Period of validity of ROFOR is
questions.cite: Validity period read from coded ROFOR group; times are UTC.

questions.q: Wind speed in ROFOR is in
questions.cite: Upper-wind speeds in Indian ROFOR are encoded in knots.

questions.q: Base of CB cloud is
questions.cite: CB base height read from coded cloud group not provided.

questions.q: Height of Freezing Level?
questions.cite: Freezing level height read from coded message not provided; 1.7 km distractor is far lower.

questions.q: Icing group in the ROFOR is
questions.cite: Icing group begins with indicator figure 6; identified from coded message.

questions.q: Type of Icing?
questions.cite: Icing-type digit decoded from coded icing group not provided.

questions.q: Indicator figure for turbulence group in the ROFOR is
questions.cite: Turbulence group indicator figure is 5 in the code table.

questions.q: Height at which Icing is expected
questions.cite: Icing height read from coded group not provided.

questions.q: Height of Icing expected to be
questions.cite: Icing layer/thickness read from coded group not provided.

questions.q: Height at which Turbulence is expected
questions.cite: Turbulence height read from coded group not provided.

questions.q: Thickness of turbulence expected is?
questions.cite: Turbulence-layer thickness read from coded group not provided.

questions.q: Wind at 5000 ft expected is?
questions.cite: Wind at 5000 ft read from coded wind group not provided.

questions.q: Wind at 20000 ft expected is?
questions.cite: Wind at 20000 ft read from coded wind group; speeds in knots.

questions.q: Temperature at 20000 ft expected is?
questions.cite: Upper-air temp read from coded temp group not provided.

questions.q: Temperature at 40,000 ft expected is?
questions.cite: Upper-air temp read from coded temp group not provided.

questions.q: Date of issue of forecast is?
questions.cite: Date read from coded header not provided; stored value retained.

questions.q: Indicator group for Jet stream in ROFOR is
questions.cite: Jet-stream indicator group taken from the coded message not provided.

questions.q: Indicator group for Maximum Wind in ROFOR is
questions.cite: Maximum-wind indicator group taken from the coded message not provided.

questions.q: Maximum Wind speed expected is
questions.cite: Max wind speed read from coded max-wind group not provided.

questions.q: Maximum Wind speed expected at height
questions.cite: Height of max wind read from coded group; only the ft option is a height value.

questions.q: Jet stream is expected at Lat/Long
questions.cite: Position read from coded jet-stream group not provided.

questions.q: Vertical Wind Shear per 300 m expected is
questions.cite: Wind-shear value read from coded group not provided.

questions.q: Jet stream core speed is expected to be
questions.cite: Jet core speed read from coded group not provided.

questions.q: Jet stream expected at height of
questions.cite: Jet-stream height read from coded group not provided.

questions.q: Wind at 40,000 ft expected is?
questions.cite: Wind at 40000 ft read from coded wind group; speeds in knots.

questions.q: Who prepares National SIGWX Charts?
questions.cite: National (low-level) significant weather charts are prepared by the national Meteorological Watch Offices; WAFC handles global high-level charts.

questions.q: Flight Level of freezing Level is included in ………… SIGWX Charts.
questions.cite: The 0°C freezing level is depicted on low-level significant weather charts, which serve flights below the mid/high-level regime.

questions.q: Fog, Precipitation and weather which reduce visibility below 5000 m is considered Significant weather for
questions.cite: Visibility below 5000 m from fog/precipitation is significant weather relevant to low-level flight operations.

questions.q: Briefing and Consultation are generally provided to aircrew ……… hours prior to the scheduled departure.
questions.cite: Standard pre-flight briefing/consultation is provided up to about 3 hours before scheduled departure.

questions.q: SIGMET information is provided to
questions.cite: SIGMET warns of en-route hazardous phenomena at all levels and is issued to flights at all levels.

questions.q: For Low Level flights, and those under Visual Flight Rules, briefing is given up to
questions.cite: Low-level/VFR briefing extends up to FL100, and up to FL150 (or higher) in mountainous terrain.

questions.q: The height indications in Flight Documentation in all en-route Met conditions
questions.cite: En-route meteorological conditions in flight documentation are expressed in Flight Levels.

questions.q: The height indications in Flight Documentation in all aerodrome Met conditions
questions.cite: Aerodrome meteorological conditions are given as heights above aerodrome elevation.

questions.q: For National Flights the Documents provided are
opts: WAFC upper wind and temp. charts only
Both WAFC upper wind and temp. charts and National SIGWX charts
questions.cite: National flight documentation supplies both WAFC upper-wind/temperature charts and national SIGWX charts.

questions.q: For National Flights the winds and temperatures are provided for LL Flights for altitudes
questions.cite: Low-level upper-wind/temperature data are provided at the standard 600, 1500 and 3000 m altitudes (garbled '300 m' repaired to '3000 m').
